communication_style.decision_style: Prefers concise recommendations with total price, timing, cabin, and key hotel amenities verified; asks targeted follow-up questions when a listing is ambiguous.
communication_style.request_pattern: Usually provides dates, destination, and fixed commitments up front, then asks for a small comparison set with the decisive tradeoffs made explicit.

habit_interactions: For flights, morning timing and current-trip feasibility define the viable set before price becomes the ranking criterion.

Business class is most salient on work trips where it is available and feasible, but its coach fallback prevents it from blocking an otherwise workable itinerary; among acceptable cabin options, lower price still matters.
United is useful from her San Francisco base but remains a soft inclusion preference, so schedule, feasibility, and price can readily move another carrier ahead.
Hotel rating thresholds shape the shortlist for nicer leisure stays or explicitly budget-focused searches, while wellness facilities distinguish otherwise suitable properties.
The coffee-maker and mini-fridge preference is a practical cross-context room default, but it is less important than location, schedule, or an applicable quality floor.

habits.boundary_condition: Apply only as a general time-of-day preference without inferring a route, date, or leg-specific requirement.
habits.condition: When choosing a flight departure time and no trip-specific timing constraint overrides the preference.
habits.exception_condition: Follow an explicitly stated timing requirement for the current trip; no reusable fallback is established when morning options are unavailable.
habits.name: prefer_morning_flight_departures
habits.scope_condition: Recurring work and leisure flight searches when no meeting, event, or same-day obligation imposes another departure period.

habits.boundary_condition: Do not let price override explicit requirements such as Wi-Fi, acceptable layover length, nonstop service when requested, or required departure and return timing.
habits.condition: When comparing flights that meet the trip's required timing, connectivity, and onboard-feature needs.
habits.default_action: Rank acceptable options by price and choose the cheapest one.
habits.exception_condition: Choose a more expensive option when the cheapest violates a stated must-have or has an unacceptably long or inconvenient layover.
habits.name: Cheapest acceptable flight
habits.preference_value: Prefer the lowest-priced flight that still satisfies essential itinerary and amenity constraints.
habits.scope_condition: Flight decisions after the current trip's timing, routing, cabin, and onboard requirements have established which itineraries are acceptable.

habits.boundary_condition: Do not rank United above other preferred carriers solely from this habit; the evidence only establishes repeated inclusion in multi-carrier sets.
habits.condition: When searching for commercial flights and no current-trip instruction specifies a different carrier set.
habits.default_action: Include United among the preferred carrier options when it is otherwise suitable and comparable.
habits.exception_condition: Use other carriers when United is unavailable, unsuitable for the itinerary, materially worse, or excluded by a current-trip instruction.
habits.name: united_soft_carrier_option
habits.preference_value: United is a recurring acceptable carrier to include among preferred flight options, but is not required or uniquely favored.
habits.scope_condition: Commercial flight searches, especially those originating from her San Francisco home base, when the trip does not specify or exclude particular carriers.

habits.boundary_condition: Treat business class as a soft preference, not a requirement, and do not infer an independent standing budget or price threshold.
habits.default_action: Prefer or surface business-class options first.
habits.exception_condition: Use coach when business class is unavailable, infeasible under explicit current-trip constraints, or declined by the user.
habits.name: prefer_business_class_with_coach_fallback
habits.preference_value: Prefer business class when available and feasible, with coach acceptable as a fallback.
habits.scope_condition: Cabin comparisons for employer-funded audit, supplier, and professional-event travel where an upgraded cabin can reasonably be considered.

habits.boundary_condition: Use a 3.5 minimum when the search is explicitly budget-focused. Apply either threshold only to the rating metric under discussion, and do not conflate hotel class, Google ratings, and customer-review ratings.
habits.condition: When a hotel search calls for a well-rated property and frames the stay as nice, upscale, resort-style, or explicitly budget-focused.
habits.default_action: Filter or prioritize options meeting a 4.0 minimum for nice, upscale, or resort-style searches, and identify the rating source when known.
habits.exception_condition: Follow any newly stated threshold or metric. If no suitable option meets the applicable floor while satisfying more important trip constraints, ask before relaxing it.
habits.name: contextual_hotel_rating_floor
habits.preference_value: Prefer hotels rated at least 4.0 when seeking a nice, upscale, or resort-style stay; for explicitly budget-focused searches, prefer at least 3.5.
habits.scope_condition: Leisure and occasional professional-event hotel searches explicitly framed as nice, upscale, resort-style, or budget-focused.

habits.boundary_condition: Do not infer preferences for other room amenities, hotel types, destinations, dates, or prices.
habits.condition: When searching for or comparing hotel rooms.
habits.default_action: Use both an in-room coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge as soft amenity criteria.
habits.exception_condition: If otherwise suitable options lack either amenity, confirm whether the preference should be relaxed rather than automatically rejecting them.
habits.name: Prefer an in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge
habits.preference_value: Prefer hotel rooms with both a coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge.
habits.scope_condition: Hotel-room comparisons for multi-night work stays and shared leisure trips when room amenity details are available.

habits.boundary_condition: Treat the pool and exercise facility as the durable core preference and the hot tub as a softer additional preference. Do not infer indoor versus outdoor pool requirements, a specific pool type, or unrelated room amenities unless stated for the current trip.
habits.condition: When choosing or comparing hotels based on wellness or recreation amenities.
habits.default_action: Prioritize hotels that offer both a pool and an on-site fitness center, gym, or comparable exercise facility; among otherwise suitable options, prefer one that also has a hot tub.
habits.exception_condition: Relax the hot-tub preference when it materially limits suitable options, and relax either core amenity when the user explicitly waives it or stronger current-trip constraints favor another hotel.
habits.name: prefers_hotels_with_pool_fitness_and_optional_hot_tub
habits.preference_value: Prefer hotels with both a pool and an on-site fitness facility, with a hot tub as an additional preference when available.
habits.scope_condition: Shared leisure stays where Priya and her spouse expect to exercise or spend downtime at the property.

longitudinal_plan.travel_tempo: Two or three work-travel planning episodes in many months, interspersed with conference trips, itinerary changes, and several more deliberate leisure-planning episodes each year.
longitudinal_plan.typical_episode_shape: A work episode usually begins with fixed site dates and arrival requirements, proceeds through one or two flight-shortlist revisions, and ends with a practical hotel check. Leisure episodes unfold over more sessions, with destination or date exploration followed by repeated hotel comparisons, amenity verification, and occasional flight repricing.

persona.household: Lives with her spouse; they take several long-weekend wellness trips and one longer resort vacation most years.
persona.name: Priya Nair
persona.planning_behavior: She establishes immovable audit or personal dates first, then narrows flights by departure time, cabin feasibility, and carrier practicality before comparing the acceptable options by price. She makes work decisions from concise shortlists and is willing to use coach when an upgrade is impractical. For leisure hotels, she compares ratings and wellness amenities carefully, while practical in-room conveniences remain useful across both work and personal stays.
persona.travel_pattern: Priya travels two or three times in many months to audit manufacturing sites, qualify suppliers, and attend quality leadership meetings across the United States. Most work trips last two to four nights and have fixed on-site start times. She also plans quieter leisure stays with her spouse, often at coastal or resort destinations where hotel amenities matter more than they do during audits.

travel_contexts.description: Frequent two- to four-night domestic trips built around fixed morning audit starts, employer travel rules, and a need to arrive rested.
Occasional conferences and quality leadership meetings with somewhat more flexible schedules but the same cost-conscious booking process.
Several shared leisure trips each year, commonly coastal or resort-oriented, where property quality and wellness facilities receive more attention.
